title: From a grill demonstration to a trademark file
lede: Thirty moments, with the rivals alongside. Where sources disagree on a date or a count, the entry says so.

events.title: General Equipment founded
events.text: Frank Thomas Sr. starts a company making frozen custard and ice cream machines. One history dates it to 1929.

events.title: The flame broiler
events.text: Frank Thomas Jr. agrees to mass-produce flame broilers for a Miami-based chain and to market them outside Florida.

events.title: Pilot stand at Little America
events.text: A demonstration hamburger stand opens at an Indianapolis amusement park. The Indianapolis Star counts this as the first Burger Chef.

events.title: First Burger Chef
events.text: Opens at 1300 West 16th Street, Indianapolis, with Robert Wildman as partner.

events.title: Eight restaurants, or forty
events.text: The Encyclopedia of Indianapolis counts eight in three states. The Indianapolis Star says more than 40 by October.

events.title: About 70 restaurants
events.text: Two years after launch, according to the Indianapolis Business Journal.

events.title: The Big Shef
events.text: A double-decker burger with cheese, lettuce and sauce. Sources give 1964 or 1965.

events.title: Downtown Indianapolis
events.text: The first downtown restaurant opens at 6 East Washington Street. One history numbers it store 450.

events.title: About 500 restaurants
events.text: The Encyclopedia of Indianapolis says 500; the Business Journal says 440.

events.title: Pillsbury buys Burger King
events.text: The chain has 274 stores and is valued at $18 million.

events.title: Second-largest chain
events.text: Burger Chef trails only McDonald’s.

events.title: Sold to General Foods
events.text: $16 million for about 700 owned and franchised units, by the Times account. Other reports range up to $25 million.

events.title: McDonald’s opens its 1,000th restaurant
events.text: The leader passes four figures in the year Burger Chef is sold.

events.title: 1,000th Burger Chef
events.text: One year after the sale.

events.title: First Wendy’s
events.text: Opens in Columbus, Ohio.

events.title: The peak
events.text: About 1,200 restaurants. McCann Erickson resigns the advertising account and Ogilvy & Mather takes it.

events.title: An $83 million loss
events.text: General Foods discloses the loss, mostly on Burger Chef. The after-tax charge is $46.8 million.

events.title: The president retires
events.text: Arthur E. Larkin Jr. leaves General Foods at 55.

events.title: Closures
events.text: More than 100 units closed, all Rix roast-beef units to go, and a net reduction of 25% planned.

events.title: The Funmeal
events.text: A boxed meal for children with puzzles and stories.

events.title: Star Wars Funmeal
events.text: Seven trays with punch-out toys, made with Coca-Cola under license from Twentieth Century-Fox.

events.title: Speedway
events.text: Four employees are abducted from the Speedway, Indiana restaurant and found dead two days later. The case is unsolved.

events.title: The Happy Meal
events.text: McDonald’s introduces its own children’s meal. Burger Chef sues.

events.title: “Barely a breakeven operation”
events.text: The Times’ description of Burger Chef, by then a regional chain.

events.title: Sale to Hardee’s reported
events.text: About $44 million. General Foods expects a charge of about 25 cents a share.

events.title: Conversions in Indianapolis
events.text: A television report covers 75 local restaurants becoming Hardee’s.

events.title: The last Burger Chef
events.text: The Cookeville, Tennessee franchise becomes “Pleasers.”

events.title: Trademark challenged
events.text: River West Brands petitions to cancel two Burger Chef registrations as abandoned.

events.title: The Big Shef returns
events.text: Hardee’s sells it for a limited time in five Indiana and Ohio markets.

events.title: Challenge withdrawn
events.text: River West files a withdrawal of its petition.

events.title: Another limited run
events.text: Hardee’s serves the Big Shef again in Indianapolis while the chain appears in the television series Mad Men.
